assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Aharonov–Bohm effect and Berry phase established that quantum phase has direct physical consequences and revealed a broad geometric structure underlying quantum mechanics.
assessment.attribution: Aharonov and Bohm articulated the effect; Berry identified the general geometric phase. The credited pair captures central theoretical contributions, though the discovery's experimental history is broader.
assessment.maturity: These ideas have been tested across many systems and are deeply embedded in modern physics.
uncertainties: The proposed scope combines related but distinct contributions, and the division of credit for the Aharonov–Bohm effect extends beyond the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Effective-one-body theory and numerical relativity made reliable predictions for binary black-hole mergers possible, enabling gravitational-wave observations to test strong-field gravity.
assessment.attribution: Damour and Buonanno developed the effective-one-body framework; Pretorius demonstrated stable numerical merger simulations. Together they represent complementary theoretical advances.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been validated against observed merger signals and now support a mature field of gravitational-wave astronomy.
uncertainties: Many researchers contributed to the modeling, and the boundary between these foundational advances and later waveform development is not sharp.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The titanium-sapphire laser and practical passive mode-locking enabled reliable femtosecond pulses, opening a wide range of ultrafast experiments, including time-resolved studies of atomic and molecular processes.
assessment.attribution: Moulton's laser medium and the distinct mode-locking approaches associated with Keller and Sibbett form a coherent set of contributions. The broader development involved additional groups and engineering work.
assessment.maturity: The laser platform has been widely reproduced, refined, and used for decades.
uncertainties: The discovery groups' relative contributions to the enabling laser technology and its mode-locking methods may be difficult to separate cleanly.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks have brought timekeeping to extraordinary precision and opened sensitive tests of fundamental physics, including measurements of gravitational redshift over small height differences.
assessment.attribution: Katori introduced the lattice clock concept and demonstrated its key trapping strategy; Ye's work drove major advances in implementation, precision, and applications.
assessment.maturity: Independent laboratory development and sustained improvements show strong reproducibility and a clear record of scientific use.
uncertainties: Clock performance continues to improve, so the eventual scientific scope of the technique is still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The recollision model explained how strong laser fields drive high-harmonic generation and rescattering, giving attosecond science a predictive theoretical foundation.
assessment.attribution: The credited physicists made central theoretical contributions to the model and its development. Corkum also connected the picture closely to experimental strong-field physics.
assessment.maturity: The model has been tested and extended across a broad range of strong-field and attosecond experiments.
uncertainties: The model emerged through contributions from multiple groups, and its relationship to the experimental advances recognized by the 2023 Physics Prize complicates the scope of a separate award.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of pulsars revealed a new class of compact astrophysical objects and provided precise probes of gravity, dense matter, and stellar evolution.
assessment.attribution: Bell Burnell identified the unusual radio signal in the discovery data. The credited attribution recognizes that decisive work, while the wider discovery depended on a research team.
assessment.maturity: Pulsars have been observed in large numbers and have become indispensable tools across astrophysics.
uncertainties: The circumstances of discovery and allocation of credit among Bell Burnell, her supervisors, and the team remain historically contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution made quantum measurement and entanglement operational resources for secure communication and helped establish quantum information as a physical research field.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard introduced the influential BB84 protocol; Ekert's entanglement-based proposal was a distinct foundational contribution also represented on the ballot.
assessment.maturity: The principles have been repeatedly demonstrated, and quantum key distribution has progressed to real communication networks.
uncertainties: The eventual practical reach of quantum cryptography remains unsettled, and selecting particular protocols risks underrepresenting parallel foundational work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light reduces quantum noise in precision measurements and has become an important tool for gravitational-wave detectors and other interferometers.
assessment.attribution: Caves established key theoretical limits and strategies; Kimble helped develop the experimental foundation; Mavalvala led influential application in gravitational-wave detection.
assessment.maturity: Squeezed-light techniques have been demonstrated repeatedly and used in operating gravitational-wave observatories.
uncertainties: The field includes substantial contributions from several experimental groups, including work represented by Roman Schnabel, so a three-person attribution is necessarily selective.
